messages:
sam_g: quick question on eviction grace vs admission safety — we're seeing tenants hit short bursts and then immediately get evicted which kills KV cache effectiveness and spikes p95. is anyone thinking of separating the admission surface (who gets a new lease) from eviction grace (how long we keep warm state) so costs and latency don't oscillate

maria_k: yeah i've been noodling that. two planes: admission = headroom+burs t_credits check + cost band sanity; eviction = soft-grace window + reclaim signals. keep admission conservative, give eviction a soft TTL so caches survive short churn :wave:

jay_p: can we formalize the signals? e.g. admission should see: available_gpus, reserved_headroom, tenant_priority, burst_tokens. eviction should see: lease_age, keep_kv_cache flag, reclaim_urgency. otherwise autoscaler and reconciler thrash each other

anya: +1. proposal sketch: extend lease metadata with fields: `priority_class`, `burst_tokens_remaining`, `prewarm_hint_ms`, `min_reservation_ms`, `keep_kv_cache` (bool). example config snippet: ```yaml
# lease metadata example
priority_class: standard
burst_tokens_remaining: 120
prewarm_hint_ms: 5000
min_reservation_ms: 60000
keep_kv_cache: true
```

maria_k: operationally we should also split responsibilities: autoscaler -> emits an "Intent" object (scale intent + admission decision). operator/controller -> validates intent against local constraints (node labels, cost bands), then performs allocation. this way autoscaler can be aggressive in predictions but controller applies safety checks to avoid cross-tenant cost bleed

sam_g: sounds good. one open Q: how do we charge for prewarm capacity? do we bill prewarm as reserved capacity (amortized) or meter only active tokens? affects pricing and tenant choices for prewarm_hint_ms

jay_p: i'd push hybrid: small amortized prewarm fee (keeps infra honest) + metered consumption once actual tokens consumed. simplifies cost forecasting for tenants that rely on prewarm a lot

ops-bot: deploy-bot: applied `lease-metadata` feature flag to staging (rollout=10%) — watch for eviction regressions. :robot_face:

anya: implementation detail: eviction path should accept an annotation `keep_kv_cache=true` plus `grace_ms`. eviction flow: if reclaim_urgency < threshold and keep_kv_cache true -> mark node as recycled but preserve KV for grace_ms, do not reassign memory immediately. prevents wasted loads on model cache and reduces tail latency

maria_k: compatibility note: default must keep current behavior. new fields behind `lease-metadata-v2` feature flag. add telemetry: count of prevented evictions and cache-preserved seconds so we can validate SLO impact

sam_g: on operator shim changes — what exact fields do we need in the reconciler API? also need stable annotations so older controllers ignore unknown keys

anya: shim API minimal fields: `intent_id`, `tenant_id`, `lease_id`, `priority_class`, `requested_gpus`, `burst_tokens`, `prewarm_hint_ms`, `min_reservation_ms`, `keep_kv_cache`. optional: `cost_center` and `amortized_preload_fee`. example tiny payload: ```json
{"intent_id":"i-123","tenant_id":"t-45","lease_id":"l-9","priority_class":"standard","requested_gpus":1,"burst_tokens":60,"prewarm_hint_ms":2000,"keep_kv_cache":true}
```

jay_p: i'll draft an RFC that covers: admission intent schema, controller validation rules, eviction grace semantics, and billing model. seeking reviewers: @maria_k @anya @sam_g — aiming to publish EOD friday. :thumbsup:

maria_k: happy to review. can you include a short experiment plan: staging rollout, metrics to watch (p95 latency, cache-hit-duration, tenant cost delta)

sam_g: yes please include rollback criteria. also add a small load test sim that alternates bursts every 30s to expose thrash

ops-bot: incident-bot: created task INC-2026-78 to track rollout observability for lease-metadata-v2

sam_g: thanks all. if we can get the RFC up today i'll schedule a quick sync tomorrow to nail tuning knobs. :rocket:
